original_test_intent: Confirm that the temperature sensor belonging to the installed DCSCM module is correctly represented and readable in SDR, IPMI Sensor List and BMC Web, with the expected identity, measurement semantics and value under the recorded operating condition.
original_method: Bind TEMP_DCSCM to the exact module/FRU and sensing point, preserve the current log baseline, collect complete in-band and out-of-band IPMI records, capture the matching Web row and compare capability-aware fields against the versioned DCSCM specification.
manual_activity: The platform owner identifies the installed DCSCM module and sensor semantics, supplies expected fields and confirms the corresponding BMC Web row. Automation may collect and compare the read-only IPMI objects.
required_inputs: DCSCM module PN/revision/serial or unique FRU identity and physical location
BMC/SDR/firmware version and stable TEMP_DCSCM record locator
Whether the sensor measures module silicon, board-local, inlet or ambient temperature
Expected name, description, entity, units, scaling, status and supported thresholds
Expected operating range for the recorded ambient/load state and freshness/update interval
Trusted in-band and OOB IPMI identities and allowed presentation tolerance
BMC Web label/field/rounding map to the same record
Log-retention, anomaly and independent recovery policy
safety_requirements: Do not merge the duplicate code's CPU-temperature result with this DCSCM result
Verify the sensor belongs to the named DCSCM instance rather than accepting a label match alone
Use full raw SDR and Sensor List output before filtering; do not truncate to 100 lines
Keep the operation read-only and do not force temperature, alter thresholds, fans, firmware or BMC settings
Preserve dmesg, syslog and SEL instead of clearing them automatically
Keep credentials out of command arguments and redact retained evidence
Stop on stale/unavailable/unitless data, IB/OOB disagreement, thermal anomaly or management-path instability
agent_execution_scope: Fingerprint the DCSCM FRU and bind its sensor locator
Collect complete in-band and OOB SDR/Sensor List data through approved paths
Extract TEMP_DCSCM with entity, units, value, status, thresholds and timestamp
Compare both IPMI paths and prepare the mapped Web fields for operator confirmation
Evaluate capability-aware specification and operating-envelope rules
Do not apply stimulus, writes or a formal verdict
engineer_actions: Approve DCSCM component and sensing-point identity
Provide field semantics, capability, range and freshness oracle
Confirm Web mapping and allowable rounding/poll delay
Review anomalies and issue the verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The exact `sensor get TEMP_DCSCM` can contribute evidence after identity is proven, but it omits the source's in-band path and Web comparison. Its password argument and truncated fallback are unacceptable, and a numeric value alone is not the required specification comparison.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Collect complete supported in-band and secret-safe OOB SDR/Sensor List data, resolve the exact TEMP_DCSCM record by component/entity, retain all fields, and compare it with the mapped BMC-Web row and versioned DCSCM sensor specification.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: TEMP_DCSCM, IB/OOB commands, BMC Web Sensor list, field-to-SPEC criteria and 3/3-minute estimates remain. The malformed `lanplus-C` token is treated as a transcription defect, not executed literally.

modernized_recommendation.status: REQUIRES DCSCM SENSOR PROVENANCE AND SPECIFICATION
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Tie the DCSCM FRU to its sensor entity, capture full IB/OOB representations and the Web row at aligned timestamps, normalize units/rounding/poll delay, compare only supported fields and record the environmental context.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds module/sensing-point provenance, capability-aware comparison and safe retention while preserving the three source views.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A label and one OOB value cannot prove correct DCSCM association, in-band parity or Web presentation. A CPU-temperature result under the duplicate code is also non-transferable.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Polling delays and rounding may produce benign small differences; identity or stale-data errors are more serious because they can hide DCSCM overheating.

project_override_considerations: If a platform exposes multiple DCSCM instances or renamed sensors, the owner must list each applicable component and mapping. Unsupported thresholds may be marked not implemented with specification evidence; they must not be invented or treated as zero.
expected_evidence: Exact source variant and explicit separation from row-1651 CPU management
DCSCM FRU/module/sensing-point and BMC/SDR firmware identity
Full redacted IB and OOB SDR and Sensor List outputs with timestamps and exit status
Resolved TEMP_DCSCM record including entity, units, reading, status and supported thresholds
Timestamped BMC-Web row plus normalized parity analysis
Operating context and baseline/post dmesg/syslog/SEL/BMC health without unapproved clearing

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: This exact row consistently defines TEMP_DCSCM across Items, procedure and criteria. Reuse of the code by the earlier AMD CPU-temperature row is isolated through source identity and does not make this row internally contradictory.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The passive sensor comparison is clear and bounded. Exact module, sensor semantics and expected values are normal platform inputs that can be provided before execution, so no permanent blocker remains.

review_improvement: Makes DCSCM component and sensing-point provenance the center of the check, retains all three required views and prevents either a truncated OOB reading or the duplicate CPU case from being accepted as complete evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: A stable label is insufficient when the same code has already caused DCSCM data to leak into a CPU test. This row must prove the reverse direction: the record actually belongs to the installed DCSCM and represents the documented thermal point. Full IB/OOB objects and the Web row can be normalized despite polling delay, but only against an owner-supplied component specification; passive collection then becomes safely automatable with confirmation.
